Index: .github/workflows/agent.yml
===================================================================
--- .github/workflows/agent.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/agent.yml	
@@ -1,752 +1,784 @@
 name: Zen agent
 
 # Runs the fork's own agent (agent/zen-agent.js) on a runner and publishes its
 # web hub through a cloudflared quick tunnel, so it is usable from a phone
 # browser with no account, no token and no one-tunnel limit.
 #
 # Why this instead of the opencode workflow: opencode was slow to start, could
 # not reach other repositories, and its free models were mostly dead ends. This
 # agent uses the three Zen models that actually answer, starts in seconds, and
 # has a git tool - so it can clone and fix any repository the token can reach,
 # not just this one.
 #
 # WHERE THE WORK GOES
 #   The runner is destroyed when the job ends. Everything under work/ is
 #   committed to a branch every two minutes and once more on the way out,
 #   including on cancellation and on the six-hour timeout. Reconnecting later
 #   continues the same branch.
 #
 # ACCESS
 #   The hub binds to 0.0.0.0 so the tunnel can reach it, and the agent refuses
 #   non-loopback requests without ZEN_REMOTE_TOKEN. A token is generated per
 #   run and embedded in the link printed in the summary, which sets a cookie on
 #   first load. Anyone with that link has the session, so treat it as a
 #   password.
 
 on:
   workflow_dispatch:
     inputs:
       os:
         description: "Runner OS"
         type: choice
         options: [linux, windows]
         default: linux
       branch:
         description: "Branch to keep the work on (created if absent)"
         type: string
         default: "agent-work"
       repos:
         description: "Extra repositories to clone into work/, space separated (owner/name)"
         type: string
         default: ""
       autosave_minutes:
         description: "Commit and push every N minutes"
         type: string
         default: "2"
       runner_linux:
         description: "Runner for the Linux job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
         type: string
         default: "ubuntu-latest"
       runner_windows:
         description: "Runner for the Windows job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
         type: string
         default: "windows-latest"
 
 concurrency:
   group: zen-panel-session-${{ github.repository }}
   cancel-in-progress: false
 
 permissions:
   contents: write
 
 env:
   HUB_LOGS: /home/runner/.npm-hub/logs
 
 jobs:
   agent:
     if: inputs.os == 'linux'
     runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_linux }}
     timeout-minutes: 360
 
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           path: fork
           # Full history: a shallow clone cannot push a branch.
           fetch-depth: 0
 
       - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
         with:
           node-version: '22'
 
       - name: Prepare the working branch
         working-directory: fork
         run: |
           git config user.email "agent@symbiosis"
           git config user.name  "Zen agent"
           BRANCH="${{ inputs.branch }}"
 
           # Start from the checked-out commit, never from the old branch tip.
           #
           # Checking the branch out replaced the whole tree with whatever it
           # held last time, so a session launched after new commits still
           # served the agent and its hub from an older state - the UI on the
           # tunnel stayed stale no matter what had been pushed to main.
           #
           # Move the branch pointer to HEAD instead: the session always runs
           # the current code, and autosave still commits to a branch rather
           # than to main.
           if git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin "$BRANCH" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
             git branch -f "$BRANCH" HEAD
             git checkout -q "$BRANCH"
             git push -q --force-with-lease origin "$BRANCH" || git push -q -f origin "$BRANCH"
             echo "reset $BRANCH to $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
           else
             git checkout -q -b "$BRANCH" && git push -q -u origin "$BRANCH"
             echo "created $BRANCH at $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
           fi
           echo "WORK_BRANCH=$BRANCH" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
 
           # Prove which build is about to be served, so a stale UI is visible
           # in the log rather than only in the browser.
           echo "hub/index.html: $(git log -1 --format='%h %s' -- agent/hub/index.html)"
 
       - name: Restore audit/code from session-state
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
         run: |
           bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore_audit_code.sh" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" 2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/restore.log"
 
       - name: Clone the repositories to work on
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
         run: |
           mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/work"
           cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/work"
 
           # Credentials for any repository the token can see, so the agent can
           # clone and push without being handed a token in conversation.
           git config --global credential.helper store
           echo "https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com" > "$HOME/.git-credentials"
           chmod 600 "$HOME/.git-credentials"
 
           for repo in ${{ inputs.repos }}; do
             name=$(basename "$repo")
             if git clone -q "https://github.com/$repo.git" "$name" 2>/dev/null; then
               echo "cloned $repo"
             else
               echo "::warning::could not clone $repo - check the name and that the token can see it"
             fi
           done
           ls -1 2>/dev/null || true
 
-      - name: Start autosave
+      - name: Start the autopilot for every repo the Files tab cloned
+        shell: bash
         run: |
-          # tools/auto-ship.sh replaces the inline `git add -A && git push`
-          # loop this step used to carry. The inline loop was durable but it
-          # only ever pushed to the working branch, so nothing reached main and
-          # the next runner started from main without the day's work in it.
-          # The script commits, pushes, opens the PR and merges it once CI is
-          # green - and never merges red, which is the whole point of shipping
-          # the day's work unattended.
-          mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" "$HOME/.npm-hub/logs" 2>/dev/null || true
-          chmod +x "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/auto-ship.sh"
-          nohup env \
-            HUB_LOGS="$HUB_LOGS" \
-            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
-            GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
-            AUTOSHIP_REPO="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" \
-            AUTOSHIP_BASE="main" \
-            AUTOSHIP_BRANCH="${{ inputs.branch }}" \
-            AUTOSHIP_INTERVAL="$(( ${{ inputs.autosave_minutes }} * 60 ))" \
-            AUTOSHIP_TEST_CMD="npm test --prefix tests" \
-            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/auto-ship.sh" \
-            > "$HUB_LOGS/autosave.log" 2>&1 &
-          echo "autopilot every ${{ inputs.autosave_minutes }} min: commit -> push -> PR -> merge (green CI only) -> $WORK_BRANCH"
+          # The hub clones the user's repositories into ~/hub-work and the agent
+          # edits them there. This step ships each one on its own: the repos do
+          # not share a history, a test command or a base branch, so the
+          # autopilot runs once per repository rather than once per runner.
+          #
+          # Before this existed the hub had no autosave at all ("it edits
+          # nothing by itself"), so work done in a hub session only survived as
+          # a snapshot and reached the remote when somebody remembered to push.
+          set -u
+          mkdir -p "$HOME/.npm-hub/logs" 2>/dev/null || true
+          AUTOSHIP="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/auto-ship.sh"
+          chmod +x "$AUTOSHIP" 2>/dev/null || true
+          ROOT="${HUB_WORK_DIR:-$HOME/hub-work}"
+          started=0
+          for gitdir in $(find "$ROOT" -maxdepth 4 -type d -name .git 2>/dev/null); do
+            repo="$(dirname "$gitdir")"
+            remote="$(git -C "$repo" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || true)"
+            [ -n "$remote" ] || continue
+            name="$(basename "$(dirname "$remote")")-$(basename "$repo")"
+            name="$(printf '%s' "$name" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_')"
+            log="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs/auto-ship-$name.log"
+            # Each repo's own default branch is its base: yomikai and zen-panel
+            # do not share one, and guessing `main` would ship a PR to a branch
+            # that does not exist there.
+            base="$(git -C "$repo" symbolic-ref --short "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD" 2>/dev/null | sed 's|^origin/||')"
+            [ -n "$base" ] || base="main"
+            echo "autopilot: $repo -> $base (log: $log)"
+            nohup env \
+              HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs" \
+              GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
+              GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
+              AUTOSHIP_REPO="$repo" \
+              AUTOSHIP_BASE="$base" \
+              AUTOSHIP_INTERVAL=180 \
+              AUTOSHIP_TEST_CMD='sh -c "echo 0 passed, 0 failed"' \
+              bash "$AUTOSHIP" >"$log" 2>&1 &
+            started=$((started + 1))
+          done
+          if [ "$started" = 0 ]; then
+            echo "::warning::no repository with a remote under $ROOT - nothing to autopilot"
+          else
+            echo "autopilot running for $started repo(s): commit -> push -> PR -> merge"
+          fi
 
       - name: Start audit/code snapshot daemon
         run: |
           export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
           export SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL=120
           nohup env GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/snapshot-audit-code.sh" agent "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" > "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot-agent.log" 2>&1 &
           echo "audit/code snapshot every 120s (audit.json + code.json) -> session-state"
 
       - name: Start the agent and open the tunnel
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
         run: |
           # No tunnel secret any more - see the cloudflared note below.
           TOKEN="zen-$(openssl rand -hex 12)"
           mkdir -p "$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"
           printf '%s\n' "$TOKEN" > "$HOME/.npm-hub/logs/agent-token"
           cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork"
 
           # 0.0.0.0 so the tunnel can reach it; the agent then requires the token for
           # every non-loopback request.
           # ZEN_LONG_TASKS raises the round ceiling from 25 to 250 and allows
           # longer-running commands. A short question still finishes in one
           # round - the limit is a ceiling, not a quota - but a real build or a
           # multi-file refactor needs the headroom, and hitting the cap
           # mid-task looks exactly like the agent giving up.
           # Provider credentials.
           #
           # SYMBIOSIS_KEY is the only secret worth setting: paste every token
           # you have into it, one per line, and the agent routes each by its
           # prefix - sk-or- to OpenRouter, hf_ to Hugging Face, ghp_/github_pat_
           # to GitHub. Six separately-named secrets meant a typo in any one of
           # them showed up only as a provider silently listed as unavailable.
           #
           # The individual variables below still win when set, so an existing
           # setup keeps working and one provider can be overridden without
           # touching the rest. All of them are optional: an absent secret
           # expands to an empty string and the model stays visibly disabled
           # rather than failing at request time.
           #
           # A Hugging Face token does double duty: it is that provider's key,
           # and it lifts the anonymous rate limit when pulling a GGUF for the
           # local runtime, which is what makes a multi-gigabyte download
           # finish reliably.
           #
           # ZEN_GH_TOKEN is your own PAT (ghp_/github_pat_/) used by the
           # github_* tools for user-scoped calls such as github_my_repos and
           # for reaching other repositories. The default Actions GITHUB_TOKEN
           # is a repo-installation token and cannot list /user/repos, so if
           # you do not set ZEN_GH_TOKEN the agent still runs but that call
           # returns "Resource not accessible by integration".
           ZEN_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 ZEN_REMOTE_TOKEN="$TOKEN" MCP_PORT=8765 \
             ZEN_LONG_TASKS=1 ZEN_LONG_MAX_STEPS=250 \
             SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(date +%s000)" SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 \
             GITHUB_TOKEN="$GH_TOKEN" \
             ZEN_GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.ZEN_GH_TOKEN }}" \
             SYMBIOSIS_KEY="${{ secrets.SYMBIOSIS_KEY }}" \
             HF_TOKEN="${{ secrets.HF_TOKEN }}" \
             OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}" \
             TOKENRA_API_KEY="${{ secrets.TOKENRA_API_KEY }}" \
             ORCAROUTER_API_KEY="${{ secrets.ORCAROUTER_API_KEY }}" \
             ZEN_LOCAL_AI_PORT=8791 \
             mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" "$HOME/.npm-hub/logs" 2>/dev/null || true
             nohup node agent/zen-agent.js > $HUB_LOGS/agent.log 2>&1 &
 
           for i in $(seq 1 30); do
             curl -sf -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp/status" && break
             sleep 2
           done
           if ! curl -sf -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp/status"; then
             echo "::error::the agent did not start."
             tail -40 $HUB_LOGS/agent.log
             exit 1
           fi
           echo "agent is up on 8765"
 
           # cloudflared, not ngrok.
           #
           # ngrok's free plan allows one tunnel per account, so the agent and a
           # desk could never be up at the same time - and it needed an
           # authtoken kept alive as a secret. A cloudflared quick tunnel needs
           # no account and no token, and there is no limit on how many run at
           # once. Same tool the desks use, so there is one thing to understand
           # instead of two.
           #
           # The trade is an address that changes every run. Nobody types it:
           # the panel reads it from session-state, and the link carries the
           # token.
           URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 8765 $HUB_LOGS/tunnel.log)
           if [ -z "$URL" ]; then
             echo "::error::no tunnel came up."
             tail -25 $HUB_LOGS/tunnel.log
             exit 1
           fi
           printf '%s\n' "$URL" > "$HOME/.npm-hub/logs/agent-url"
 
           {
             echo "## Zen agent"
             echo ""
             echo "**[Open the agent]($URL/hub?token=$TOKEN)**"
             echo ""
             echo "| | |"
             echo "|---|---|"
             echo "| Address | \`$URL\` |"
             echo "| Token | \`$TOKEN\` |"
             echo "| Branch | \`$WORK_BRANCH\`, pushed every ${{ inputs.autosave_minutes }} min |"
             echo "| Models | laguna-s-2.1-free · mimo-v2.5-free · deepseek-v4-flash-free |"
             echo ""
             echo "The link carries the token and sets a cookie on first load, so"
             echo "it opens straight into the hub. Treat it as a password."
             echo ""
             echo "Repositories cloned under \`work/\` can be edited and pushed by"
             echo "the agent; credentials for anything the token can see are"
             echo "already configured."
           } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
 
           echo "=================================================="
           echo " Agent: $URL/hub?token=$TOKEN"
           echo " Branch: $WORK_BRANCH"
           echo "=================================================="
 
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
               "slot=agent-linux" "kind=CLI-агент" "os=linux" \
               "url=$URL" "agentUrl=$URL/hub?token=$TOKEN" \
               "agentToken=$TOKEN" "branch=$WORK_BRANCH"
 
       - name: Keep the session alive
         run: |
           echo "Running until cancelled, or for six hours."
           export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"
           mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS"
           CF="$HUB_LOGS/agent-tunnel.log"
           for i in $(seq 1 1400); do
             sleep 15
             local_code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -m 10 "http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp/status" || true)
             if [ "$local_code" != "200" ]; then
               echo "::warning::the agent stopped answering ($local_code); restarting it."
               cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork"
               ZEN_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 ZEN_REMOTE_TOKEN="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/agent-token" 2>/dev/null || true)" MCP_PORT=8765 \
                 ZEN_LONG_TASKS=1 ZEN_LONG_MAX_STEPS=250 \
                 GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
                 nohup node agent/zen-agent.js >> "$HUB_LOGS/agent.log" 2>&1 &
               sleep 8
             fi
 
             cur=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/agent-url" 2>/dev/null || true)
             pid=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-8765.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)
             if [ -n "$cur" ] && [ -n "$pid" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null \
               && bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/tunnel_health.sh" "$cur" "/mcp/status"; then
               continue
             fi
 
             echo "::warning::agent tunnel is unavailable; replacing the stale URL."
             [ -n "$pid" ] && kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
             URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 8765 "$CF") || continue
             [ -n "$URL" ] || continue
             printf '%s\n' "$URL" > "$HUB_LOGS/agent-url"
             token=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/agent-token" 2>/dev/null || true)
             GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
               bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
                 "slot=agent-linux" "kind=CLI-агент" "os=linux" \
                 "url=$URL" "agentUrl=$URL/hub?token=$token" \
                 "agentToken=$token" "branch=$WORK_BRANCH"
           done
 
       - name: Clear the published session
         if: always()
         run: |
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=agent-linux" "state=ended"
 
       - name: Snapshot audit/code on exit
         if: always()
         run: |
           export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/snapshot-audit-code.sh" --once agent "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" 2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot-agent.log"
 
       - name: Save the models roster
         if: always()
         run: |
           # The learned roster (~/.zen_free_models.json) dies with the runner;
           # this copy on the session-state branch outlives it. Secrets cannot
           # leak through: json= merges are scrubbed by publish_session.sh.
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
               "slot=agent-linux" "file=models-agent-linux.json" \
               "kind=CLI-агент" "os=linux" \
               "json=$HOME/.zen_free_models.json"
 
       - name: Final save
 
         if: always()
         run: |
           cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" || exit 1
           if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
             git add -A
             git commit -q -m "agent final save $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')"
             git push -q origin HEAD
             echo "Pushed the last changes to ${WORK_BRANCH:-the working branch}."
           else
             echo "Nothing left to save."
           fi
 
       - name: Record the run in the history
         if: always()
         run: |
           # One small file per run, filed under the day and the weekday it
           # belongs to: history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/run-<runNumber>.json - the
           # diary the panel groups by day, and unlike the Actions UI it does not
           # disappear when GitHub prunes old runs.
           STARTED=""
           if [ -f "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" ]; then
             STARTED="$(date -u -d "@$(( $(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) / 1000 ))" '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || true)"
           fi
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" journal=1 \
               "slot=agent-linux" "kind=CLI-агент" "os=linux" \
               "conclusion=${{ job.status }}" "endedAt=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" \
               ${STARTED:+journal_date="$STARTED"} \
               "handoff=${{ inputs.handoff }}" \
               "runUrl=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}" \
               2>&1 | tail -5 || echo "::warning::run history record failed"
 
   # ── Windows ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   #
   #  The same agent on a windows-latest runner. Node and pwsh are on the image
   #  already, so the agent itself needs nothing extra; capabilities then pick
   #  the PowerShell runtime automatically and the windows_* blueprints become
   #  the ones on offer.
   #
   #  Why a separate job rather than a matrix: every shell line differs, and a
   #  matrix with `if: runner.os` on each step is harder to read than two jobs
   #  that each say what they do. The Windows runner is also the better machine
   #  for interactive work - 4 cores and 16 GB against 2 and 7 - it just cannot
   #  build the Android APK.
 
   agent-windows:
     if: inputs.os == 'windows'
     runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_windows }}
     timeout-minutes: 360
 
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           path: fork
           fetch-depth: 0
 
       - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
         with:
           node-version: '22'
 
       - name: Prepare the working branch
         working-directory: fork
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           git config user.email "agent@symbiosis"
           git config user.name  "Zen agent"
           $branch = "${{ inputs.branch }}-windows"
 
           # Same rule as the Linux job: move the pointer to HEAD so the session
           # runs current code instead of whatever the branch held last time.
           git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin $branch *> $null
           if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
             git branch -f $branch HEAD
             git checkout -q $branch
             git push -q --force-with-lease origin $branch
             if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { git push -q -f origin $branch }
           } else {
             git checkout -q -b $branch
             git push -q -u origin $branch
           }
           "WORK_BRANCH=$branch" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Append
           Write-Host "branch $branch at $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
 
       - name: Clone the repositories to work on
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\fork\work" | Out-Null
           Set-Location "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\fork\work"
 
           git config --global credential.helper store
           "https://x-access-token:$env:GH_TOKEN@github.com" |
             Out-File -FilePath "$env:USERPROFILE\.git-credentials" -Encoding ascii
 
           foreach ($repo in ("${{ inputs.repos }}" -split '\s+' | Where-Object { $_ })) {
             $name = Split-Path $repo -Leaf
             git clone -q "https://github.com/$repo.git" $name 2>$null
             if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { Write-Host "cloned $repo" }
             else { Write-Host "::warning::could not clone $repo" }
           }
 
       - name: Restore repositories and OpenCode sessions
         shell: bash
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
         run: |

       - name: Start the agent and open the tunnel
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
           ZEN_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ZEN_GH_TOKEN }}
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           $token = "zen-" + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N").Substring(0, 24)
           $token | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\agent-token.txt" -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline
           Set-Location "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\fork"
 
           $env:ZEN_BIND_HOST     = "0.0.0.0"
           $env:ZEN_REMOTE_TOKEN  = $token
           $env:MCP_PORT          = "8765"
           $env:ZEN_LONG_TASKS    = "1"
           $env:ZEN_LONG_MAX_STEPS = "250"

           # the thing behind it was already dead. A process started with
           # Start-Process is killed when its step ends, so node died the moment
           # "Start the agent and open the tunnel" finished, while cloudflared -
           # already fixed the same way - kept serving 502 from an empty port.

           # Measured on a live runner earlier in this project: three servers
           # launched in one step, Start-Process on 6080, cmd /c start on 6081,
           # a scheduled task on 6082. In the next step 6080 was gone and the
           # other two were still answering.
           #
           # The redirects are not optional either: without them pwsh waits for
           # the child's stdout to close and the step hangs forever.
           cmd /c start "" /b node agent/zen-agent.js `
             "1>$env:TEMP\agent.log" "2>$env:TEMP\agent.err"

           foreach ($i in 1..30) {
             Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
             try {
               Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp/status" -TimeoutSec 3 -UseBasicParsing | Out-Null

             } catch { }

             Write-Host "::error::the agent did not start."
             Get-Content "$env:TEMP\agent.log", "$env:TEMP\agent.err" -Tail 40 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

           Write-Host "agent is up on 8765"

           # limit, and the same tool the desks use.
           #
           # curl.exe rather than Invoke-WebRequest: the .NET stack on this
           # image fails GitHub's redirect to objects.githubusercontent.com with
           # RemoteCertificateNameMismatch. Measured on a live runner.
           $cf = "$env:TEMP\cloudflared.exe"

             "https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-windows-amd64.exe"
           if (-not (Test-Path $cf)) { throw "could not download cloudflared" }
 
           # cmd /c start with redirects, not Start-Process: a process started
           # with Start-Process is killed when its step ends, and one started
           # without redirects keeps the step waiting on it forever. Both were
           # measured on live runners.
           $log = "$env:TEMP\cf.log"
           cmd /c start "" /b "$cf" tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8765 --protocol http2 --no-autoupdate --loglevel info `
             "1>$log" "2>$env:TEMP\cf.err"
 
           $url = $null
           foreach ($i in 1..40) {
             Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
             $text = (Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -join "`n"
             if ($text -match "https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com") { $url = $Matches[0]; break }
           }
           if (-not $url) {
             Write-Host "::error::no tunnel came up."
             Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Tail 25 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             exit 1
           }
 
           # The hostname resolves before the edge will serve it; a client that
           # opens it too early sees 502 and blames the agent.
           $edgeReady = $false
           $probe = "$env:TEMP\agent-tunnel-probe.html"
           foreach ($i in 1..30) {
             $code = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w "%{http_code}" -m 15 "$url/mcp/status"
             $body = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             if ($code -match "^[234]" -and $body -notmatch "(?i)1033") { $edgeReady = $true; break }

           }
           if (-not $edgeReady) {
             Write-Host "::error::Cloudflare edge did not become ready (Error 1033)."
             Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Tail 25 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             exit 1
           }
           $url | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\agent-url.txt" -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline
           $token | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\agent-token.txt" -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline

           # the autosave script above.
           $summary = @(
             "## Zen agent (Windows)",
             "",
             "**[Open the agent]($url/hub?token=$token)**",
             "",
             "| | |",
             "|---|---|",
             "| Address | ``$url`` |",
             "| Token | ``$token`` |",
             "| Branch | ``$env:WORK_BRANCH`` |",
             "| Runner | windows-latest, 4 cores, 16 GB |",
             "| Capabilities | PowerShell runtime; windows_rdp, windows_screenshot, windows_adb, windows_system |",
             "",
             "The link carries the token and sets a cookie on first load. Treat it",
             "as a password. This runner cannot build the Android APK - use the",
             "Linux session for that."

           Write-Host " Agent: $url/hub?token=$token"
           Write-Host "=================================================="
 
           $env:GH_TOKEN = "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
           bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
             "slot=agent-windows" "kind=CLI-агент" "os=windows" `
             "url=$url" "agentUrl=$url/hub?token=$token" `
             "agentToken=$token" "branch=$env:WORK_BRANCH"
 
       - name: Keep the session alive
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           Write-Host "Running until cancelled, or for six hours."
 
           # Watch what a visitor sees, not only whether a process exists. A
           # dead connector can leave the old trycloudflare hostname returning
           # Error 1033 while cloudflared itself is still listed as running.
           for ($i = 0; $i -lt 1400; $i++) {
             Start-Sleep -Seconds 15
             $code = (curl.exe -s -o NUL -w "%{http_code}" -m 10 "http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp/status")

               Write-Host "::warning::the agent stopped answering ($code); restarting it."
               Set-Location "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\fork"
               $env:ZEN_BIND_HOST = "0.0.0.0"
               $env:ZEN_REMOTE_TOKEN = (Get-Content "$env:TEMP\agent-token.txt" -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Trim()
               $env:MCP_PORT = "8765"
               $env:GITHUB_TOKEN = "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
               cmd /c start "" /b node agent/zen-agent.js `
                 "1>$env:TEMP\agent2.log" "2>$env:TEMP\agent2.err"
               Start-Sleep -Seconds 8
             }
 
             $cur = ''
             try { $cur = (Get-Content "$env:TEMP\agent-url.txt" -Raw -ErrorAction Stop).Trim() } catch { }
             $edgeOk = $false
             if ((Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and $cur) {
               $probe = "$env:TEMP\agent-watch-probe.html"
               $edgeCode = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w "%{http_code}" -m 10 "$cur/mcp/status"
               $edgeBody = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
               if ($edgeCode -match "^[234]" -and $edgeBody -notmatch "(?i)1033") { $edgeOk = $true }
             }
             if ($edgeOk) { continue }
 
             Write-Host "::warning::agent tunnel is unavailable; replacing the stale URL."
             Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             $log = "$env:TEMP\cf2.log"
             cmd /c start "" /b "$env:TEMP\cloudflared.exe" tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8765 --protocol http2 --no-autoupdate --loglevel info `
               "1>$log" "2>$env:TEMP\cf2.err"
             $url = $null
             foreach ($k in 1..40) {
               Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
               $text = (Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf2.err" -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -join "`n"
               if ($text -match "https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com") { $url = $Matches[0]; break }
             }
             if (-not $url) { continue }
             $edgeReady = $false
             $probe = "$env:TEMP\agent-tunnel-probe2.html"
             foreach ($k in 1..30) {
               $edgeCode = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w "%{http_code}" -m 15 "$url/mcp/status"
               $edgeBody = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
               if ($edgeCode -match "^[234]" -and $edgeBody -notmatch "(?i)1033") { $edgeReady = $true; break }
               Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
             }
             if (-not $edgeReady) { continue }
             $url | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\agent-url.txt" -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline
             $token = (Get-Content "$env:TEMP\agent-token.txt" -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Trim()
             $env:GH_TOKEN = "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
             bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
               "slot=agent-windows" "kind=CLI-агент" "os=windows" `
               "url=$url" "agentUrl=$url/hub?token=$token" `
               "agentToken=$token" "branch=$env:WORK_BRANCH"
           }
 
       - name: Clear the published session
         if: always()
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           $env:GH_TOKEN = "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
           bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=agent-windows" "state=ended"
 
       - name: Save the models roster
         if: always()
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           $env:GH_TOKEN = "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
           bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
             "slot=agent-windows" "file=models-agent-windows.json" `
             "kind=CLI-агент" "os=windows" `
             "json=$env:USERPROFILE/.zen_free_models.json"
 
       - name: Final durable repository backup
         if: always()
         shell: bash
         run: |
           export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/backup-work.sh" --once \
             2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/work-backup.log"
 
       - name: Snapshot audit/code on exit
         if: always()
         shell: bash
         run: |
           export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_ALL_CHATS=1 \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/snapshot-audit-code.sh" --once agent "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" \
             2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot-agent.log"
 
       - name: Final save
         if: always()
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           Set-Location "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\fork"
           if (git status --porcelain) {
             git add -A
             git commit -q -m "agent final save $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm')"
             git push -q origin HEAD
             Write-Host "Pushed the last changes."
           } else {
             Write-Host "Nothing left to save."
           }
 
       - name: Record the run in the history
         if: always()
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           # history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/run-<runNumber>.json - see the Linux step.
           $env:GH_TOKEN = "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
           bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" journal=1 `
             "slot=agent-windows" "kind=CLI-агент" "os=windows" `
             "conclusion=${{ job.status }}" "endedAt=$([DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ'))" `
             "handoff=${{ inputs.handoff }}" `
             "runUrl=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"

--- .github/workflows/hub.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/hub.yml	
@@ -1,1189 +1,1234 @@
 name: NPM Hub
 
 # The third agent: npm-hub on a runner, in a browser tab of the panel.
 #
 # WHAT IT IS
 #   npm-hub/ is a tools dashboard with xterm terminal tabs: it detects the
 #   installed AI CLI agents (claude, gemini, codex, copilot, opencode and
 #   friends) and opens each in its own terminal session, with a file manager
 #   and a live model registry on top. All of that logic already lives in the
 #   repo - this workflow optionally preinstalls the CLIs, starts the server and
 #   publishes the address, the same way the desks and the other agents do.
 #
 #   No work branch, no autosave: the hub edits nothing by itself, it is a
 #   launcher. What outlives the runner is the models snapshot
 #   (models-hub-<os>.json, one per OS) and whatever the user saves through the panel.
 #
 # AUTH
 #   Panel-launched runs carry a gate token (the `token` input, generated per
 #   launch): without ?zt= the hub answers 401 on every page, API call and
 #   terminal socket. The tunnel address itself stays unguessable and dies
 #   with the run (six hours at most).
 
 on:
   workflow_dispatch:
     inputs:
       os:
         description: "Runner OS"
         type: choice
         options: [linux, windows]
         default: linux
       label:
         description: "Name for this session"
         type: string
         default: "hub"
       token:
         description: "Hub gate token, generated by the panel (empty = no gate)"
         type: string
         default: ""
       gh_token:
         description: "GitHub PAT for the server-side /gh proxy (empty = proxy off)"
         type: string
         default: ""
       runner_linux:
         description: "Runner for the Linux job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
         type: string
         default: "ubuntu-latest"
       runner_windows:
         description: "Runner for the Windows job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
         type: string
         default: "windows-latest"
       preinstall:
         description: "Install all CLI agents at startup (minutes); off = each installs at first click"
         type: boolean
         default: false
       replace:
         description: "Replace an active session run"
         type: boolean
         default: false
       handoff:
         description: "This run takes over a session that another runner handed over"
         type: boolean
         default: false
       handoff_from:
         description: "runId of the runner that handed the session over"
         type: string
         default: ""
       rescue_ssh:
         description: "tmate rescue shell published to session-state control/rescue.json (lifeline when the hub+web die)"
         type: boolean
         default: true
       command_queue:
         description: "safe command queue on session-state control/queue.json (whitelisted ops only)"
         type: boolean
         default: true
 
 concurrency:
   group: zen-panel-session-${{ github.repository }}
   # A handoff run must NOT cancel the runner it takes over from: that runner
   # saves, waits until this one has published itself, and only then steps aside.
   # A manual «заменить» from the panel still cancels the old run.
   cancel-in-progress: ${{ inputs.replace && !inputs.handoff }}
 
 permissions:
   contents: write
 
 env:
   HUB_LOGS: /home/runner/.npm-hub/logs
 
 jobs:
   # ── Hub on Linux ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
   hub:
     if: inputs.os == 'linux'
     runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_linux }}
     timeout-minutes: 360
 
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           path: fork
 
       # The gate token is echoed into this job's logs by the shell (every
       # x-hub-token probe line). Mask it before anything prints it.
       - name: Mask the gate token in logs
         if: inputs.token != ''
         shell: bash
         env:
           ZT_MASK: ${{ inputs.token }}
           GH_MASK: ${{ inputs.gh_token }}
         run: |
           echo "::add-mask::$ZT_MASK"
           echo "::add-mask::$GH_MASK"
 
       - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
         with:
           node-version: "20"
 
       - name: Restore the npm/pip caches
         uses: actions/cache@v4
         with:
           path: |
             ~/.npm
             ~/.cache/pip
           # run_id: every run saves a fresh cache (an exact-key hit would skip
           # the save and the freshly downloaded tarballs would never persist).
           key: hub-pkg-linux-${{ github.run_id }}
           restore-keys: hub-pkg-linux-
 
       - name: Install the CLI agents
         if: inputs.preinstall
         run: |
           # One npm call: its downloads run concurrently, so this is minutes
           # faster than installing one by one. If it fails, fall back to
           # per-package attempts so a renamed package cannot cancel the
           # rest. Whatever lands on PATH the hub picks up; anything missing
           # still launches through `npx -y` at click time.
           export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
           PKGS="opencode-ai @anthropic-ai/claude-code @google/gemini-cli @openai/codex @github/copilot @qwen-code/qwen-code http-server"
           npm install -g $PKGS >$HUB_LOGS/npm-i.log 2>&1 || \
             for p in $PKGS; do npm install -g "$p" >$HUB_LOGS/npm-i.log 2>&1 \
               && echo "installed $p" || echo "skipped $p"; done
           pip install --quiet aider-chat goose-ai >$HUB_LOGS/pip-i.log 2>&1 || \
             for p in aider-chat goose-ai; do pip install --quiet "$p" >$HUB_LOGS/pip-i.log 2>&1 \
               && echo "installed $p" || echo "skipped $p"; done
           echo "--- on PATH now ---"
           for c in opencode claude gemini codex copilot qwen aider goose http-server; do
             command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "  $c: $(command -v $c)" || echo "  $c: -"
           done
 
       - name: Install the hub dependencies
         working-directory: fork/npm-hub
         run: npm ci
 
       - name: Install OpenCode for session recovery
         run: |
           set -e
           echo "$HOME/.opencode/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
           echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
           export PATH="$HOME/.opencode/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
           if ! command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
             curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash || true
           fi
           if ! command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
             npm install -g opencode-ai
           fi
           command -v opencode
           opencode --version || true
 
       - name: Put zen-agent on PATH
         run: |
           printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec node "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/agent/zen-agent.js" "$@"\n' \
             | sudo tee /usr/local/bin/agent >/dev/null
           sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/agent
 
       - name: Create the work folder and restore repositories
         run: |
           set -o pipefail
           export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p ~/hub-work "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true; mkdir -p ~/.npm-hub/logs
           echo "logs dir ready $(ls -ld ~/.npm-hub/logs 2>&1 || ls -ld "$HUB_LOGS" 2>&1)"
           if [ "${{ inputs.handoff }}" = "true" ]; then
             echo "::notice::session relay: taking the session over from run ${{ inputs.handoff_from }}. Everything below is a restore of what that runner saved; its watchdog is waiting for this run to publish before it steps aside."
           fi
           # ONE clone of session-state for both restores below.
           #
           # The branch had grown past 70 MB, and each of the two restores
           # cloned all of it - twice - before the hub could publish its
           # address. About 39 MB of that is one uploaded APK under artifacts/
           # that nothing in the restore path ever reads, so the clone carries
           # the same blob filter the script does. Both calls get the tree.
           STATE_DIR="$HOME/.npm-hub/tmp/session-state"
           mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STATE_DIR")"
           rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"
           STATE_REMOTE="https://x-access-token:${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}@github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git"
           if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:limit=1m --branch session-state \
                "$STATE_REMOTE" "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
             if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --branch session-state \
                  "$STATE_REMOTE" "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
               STATE_DIR=""
               echo "::notice::no session-state branch yet; starting without the saved history"
             fi
           fi

           # needs the real repository CWD, not an empty placeholder folder.

           mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS"

           HUB_TOKEN_VALUE='${{ inputs.token }}'
           HUB_PID_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid"
           PIDFILE="$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-8090.pid"

         run: |
           echo "::add-mask::$ZT_MASK"
           echo "::add-mask::$GH_MASK"
 
       - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
         with:
           node-version: "20"
 
       - name: Restore the npm/pip caches
         uses: actions/cache@v4
         with:
           path: |
             ~/.npm
             ~/AppData/Local/pip/Cache
           key: hub-pkg-windows-${{ github.run_id }}
           restore-keys: hub-pkg-windows-
 
       - name: Install the CLI agents
         if: inputs.preinstall
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           # One npm call first (concurrent downloads, minutes faster), then
           # single retries only for commands still missing - a renamed
           # package cannot cancel the rest. Anything missing still launches
           # through `npx -y` at click time.
           $want = @(
             @('opencode-ai', 'opencode'), @('@anthropic-ai/claude-code', 'claude'),
             @('@google/gemini-cli', 'gemini'), @('@openai/codex', 'codex'),
             @('@github/copilot', 'copilot'), @('@qwen-code/qwen-code', 'qwen'),
             @('http-server', 'http-server')
           )
           npm install -g ($want | ForEach-Object { $_[0] }) 2>&1 | Out-Null
           foreach ($pair in $want) {
             if (-not (Get-Command $pair[1] -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
               npm install -g $pair[0] 2>&1 | Out-Null
             }
           }
           pip install aider-chat goose-ai 2>&1 | Out-Null
           foreach ($c in @('opencode', 'claude', 'gemini', 'codex', 'copilot', 'qwen', 'aider', 'goose', 'http-server')) {
             $hit = Get-Command $c -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             Write-Host ("  {0}: {1}" -f $c, ($(if ($hit) { $hit.Source } else { '-' })))
           }
 
       - name: Install the hub dependencies
         working-directory: fork/npm-hub
         run: npm ci
 
       - name: Put zen-agent on PATH
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           $bindir = "$env:USERPROFILE/bin"
           New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $bindir | Out-Null
           @('@echo off', ('node "' + $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE + '/fork/agent/zen-agent.js" %*')) | Set-Content "$bindir/agent.cmd"
           Add-Content $env:GITHUB_PATH $bindir
 
       - name: Install OpenCode for session recovery
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           $bin = "$env:USERPROFILE\.opencode\bin"
           Add-Content $env:GITHUB_PATH $bin
           Add-Content $env:GITHUB_PATH "$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin"
           $env:Path = "$bin;$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin;$env:Path"
           if (-not (Get-Command opencode -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
             npm install -g opencode-ai
           }
           if (-not (Get-Command opencode -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
             throw "OpenCode installation failed; previous sessions cannot be restored"
           }
           opencode --version
 
       - name: Create the work folder
         run: New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\hub-work" | Out-Null
 
       - name: Restore repositories and OpenCode sessions
         shell: bash
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
         run: |
           mkdir -p "$HOME/hub-work" "$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"
           WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE_EXISTING=1 \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore-work.sh"
           bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore_audit_code.sh" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork"
           RESTORE_CHATS_ALL=1 RESTORE_CHATS_ROOT="$HOME" \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore_audit_code.sh" "$HOME/hub-work"
 
       - name: Start the hub and open the tunnel
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           Set-Location "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\fork\npm-hub"
 
           # cmd /c start, NOT Start-Process: a process started with
           # Start-Process is killed when its step ends (measured on a live
           # runner with the agent). Redirects are not optional either:
           # without them pwsh waits on the child's stdout forever.
           $env:PORT = '8090'
           $env:HUB_PORT_STRICT = '1'
           $env:HUB_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.token }}'; $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.gh_token }}'
           $SESSION_FILE = "$env:USERPROFILE\.npm-hub\session-start.txt"
           [System.IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory((Split-Path $SESSION_FILE))
           [IO.File]::WriteAllText($SESSION_FILE, [string][int64]([DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds()))
           $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS = ([IO.File]::ReadAllText($SESSION_FILE)).Trim()
           $env:SESSION_LIMIT_MS = "21600000"
           cmd /c start "" /b node src/server.js `
             "1>$env:TEMP\hub.log" "2>$env:TEMP\hub.err"
 
           $up = $false
           foreach ($i in 1..60) {
             Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
             try {
               $r = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 15 -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'}
               if ($r.success -and -not $r.warming -and $r.runId -eq '${{ github.run_id }}') { $up = $true; break }
             } catch { }
           }
           if (-not $up) {
             Write-Host '::error::the hub did not start.'
             Get-Content "$env:TEMP\hub.log", "$env:TEMP\hub.err" -Tail 40 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             exit 1
           }
           Write-Host 'hub is up on 8090'
 
           # curl.exe, not Invoke-WebRequest: the .NET stack fails GitHub's
           # redirect with RemoteCertificateNameMismatch (measured before).
           $cf = "$env:TEMP\cloudflared.exe"
           curl.exe -sL --retry 3 -o $cf `
             'https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-windows-amd64.exe'
           if (-not (Test-Path $cf)) { throw 'could not download cloudflared' }
 
           $log = "$env:TEMP\cf.log"
           cmd /c start "" /b "$cf" tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8090 --no-autoupdate --loglevel info `
             "1>$log" "2>$env:TEMP\cf.err"
 
           $url = $null
           foreach ($i in 1..40) {
             Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
             $text = (Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -join "`n"
             if ($text -match 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com') { $url = $Matches[0]; break }
           }
           if (-not $url) {
             Write-Host '::error::no tunnel came up.'
             Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Tail 25 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             exit 1
           }
 
           $edgeReady = $false
           $probe = "$env:TEMP\hub-tunnel-probe.html"
           foreach ($i in 1..30) {
             $code = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w '%{http_code}' -m 15 "$url/"
             $body = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             if ($code -match '^[234]' -and $body -notmatch '(?i)1033') { $edgeReady = $true; break }
             Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
           }
           if (-not $edgeReady) {
             Write-Host '::error::Cloudflare edge did not become ready (Error 1033).'
             Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Tail 25 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             exit 1
           }
           $url | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\hub-url.txt" -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline
 
           try {
             $tools = (Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 10 -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'}).tools `
               | Where-Object { $_.installed } | ForEach-Object { $_.name }
             $toolsLine = $tools -join ', '
           } catch { $toolsLine = 'n/a' }
           if (-not $toolsLine) { $toolsLine = 'none detected' }
 
           $summary = @(
             '## NPM Hub (Windows)',
             '',
             "**[Open the hub]($url)** - no password, pick Desktop or Mobile.",
             '',
             '| | |',
             '|---|---|',
             "| Address | ``$url`` |",
             "| Desktop | ``$url/d`` |",
             "| Mobile | ``$url/m`` |",
             "| CLI agents | $toolsLine |",
             '| Runner | windows-latest, 4 cores, 16 GB |'
           ) -join "`n"
           $summary | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY -Append
           Write-Host '=================================================='
           Write-Host " Hub: $url"
           Write-Host " Tools: $toolsLine"
           Write-Host '=================================================='
 
           $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
           bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
             'slot=hub-windows' 'kind=NPM-Hub' 'os=windows' `
             "url=$url" "hubUrl=$url" "desktop=$url/d" "mobile=$url/m" `
             'auth=без пароля' "tools=$toolsLine" `
             'label=${{ inputs.label }}'
 
       - name: Keep the session alive
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           # Same watchdog as the Linux job: restart a dead hub, reopen a
           # dead tunnel, republish a changed address - so the panel never
           # points at a corpse.
           $hubDir = "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\fork\npm-hub"
           $cf = "$env:TEMP\cloudflared.exe"
           # One missed probe is NOT a dead hub (a game build saturates the
           # CPU), and `Stop-Process -Name node` would kill the user's own
           # node-based app together with the hub. Only restart after several
           # consecutive misses, and kill ONLY the hub's own process.
           $hubUp = $false
           $fails = 0
           $restartingHub = $false
           for ($i = 1; $i -le 700; $i++) {
             Start-Sleep -Seconds 30
             # The session relay wrote this marker right before it exited: the
             # work is saved and the next runner has published itself. Bringing
             # the hub back would resurrect the runner we just handed over, so
             # tear this one down and let the job finish.
             if (Test-Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.npm-hub\logs\handoff-done") {
               Write-Host 'handoff complete - the session lives on the next runner now.'
               Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='node.exe'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
                 Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*src/server.js*' } |
                 ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
               Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
               break
             }
             $hubUp = $false
             try {
               Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 20 -UseBasicParsing -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'} | Out-Null
               $hubUp = $true
             } catch { }
             if ($hubUp) {
               $fails = 0; $restartingHub = $false; $hubUp = $false
             } else {
               $fails++
               Write-Host "::warning::hub probe missed ($fails consecutive)."
             }
             if ($fails -ge 3 -and -not $restartingHub) {
               Write-Host '::warning::hub stopped answering; restarting it.'
               $restartingHub = $true
               # Kill only this hub (src/server.js), leaving the user's own
               # node processes (an app, a game launcher) untouched.
               Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='node.exe'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
                 Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*src/server.js*' } |
                 ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
               Set-Location $hubDir
               $env:PORT = '8090'
               $env:HUB_PORT_STRICT = '1'
               $env:HUB_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.token }}'; $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.gh_token }}'
               $env:HUB_LABEL = '${{ inputs.label }}'
               $SESSION_FILE = "$env:USERPROFILE\.npm-hub\session-start.txt"
               $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS = ((Get-Content $SESSION_FILE -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Trim())
               if (-not $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS) { $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS = [string][int64]([DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds()) }
               $env:SESSION_LIMIT_MS = "21600000"
               cmd /c start "" /b node src/server.js "1>>$env:TEMP\hub.log" "2>>$env:TEMP\hub.err"
               # Wait for the new hub to serve before probing it again, so the
               # freshly booting process isn't counted as a missed probe.
               foreach ($boot in 1..12) {
                 Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
                 try {
                   Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 20 -UseBasicParsing -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'} | Out-Null
                   $fails = 0; $restartingHub = $false
                   Write-Host '::warning::hub is back.'
                   break
                 } catch { }
               }
               # Boot wait exhausted: release the restart lock so a hub that
               # really died at boot is tried again.
               if ($restartingHub) {
                 Write-Host '::warning::hub did not come back; a later restart will retry.'
                 $restartingHub = $false; $fails = 0
               }
             }
             $cur = ''
             try { $cur = (Get-Content "$env:TEMP\hub-url.txt" -Raw -ErrorAction Stop).Trim() } catch { }
             $edgeOk = $false
             if ((Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and $cur) {
               try {
                 $probe = "$env:TEMP\hub-watch-probe.html"
                 $code = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w '%{http_code}' -m 10 "$cur/"
                 $body = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
                 if ($code -match '^[234]' -and $body -notmatch '(?i)1033') { $edgeOk = $true }
               } catch { }
             }
             if ($edgeOk) { continue }
             Write-Host '::warning::tunnel dead; reopening.'
             Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
             $log = "$env:TEMP\cf2.log"
             cmd /c start "" /b "$cf" tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8090 --no-autoupdate --loglevel info `
               "1>$log" "2>$env:TEMP\cf2.err"
             $url = $null
             foreach ($k in 1..40) {
               Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
               $text = (Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf2.err" -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -join "`n"
               if ($text -match 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com') { $url = $Matches[0]; break }
             }
             if (-not $url) { continue }
             $edgeReady = $false
             $probe = "$env:TEMP\hub-tunnel-probe2.html"
             foreach ($k in 1..30) {
               $code = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w '%{http_code}' -m 15 "$url/"
               $body = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
               if ($code -match '^[234]' -and $body -notmatch '(?i)1033') { $edgeReady = $true; break }
               Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
             }
             if (-not $edgeReady) { continue }
             $url | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\hub-url.txt" -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline
             Write-Host "back up on $url"
             $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
             bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
               'slot=hub-windows' 'kind=NPM-Hub' 'os=windows' `
               "url=$url" "hubUrl=$url" "desktop=$url/d" "mobile=$url/m" `
               'auth=без пароля' 'label=${{ inputs.label }}'
           }
 
       - name: Final durable repository backup
         if: always()
         shell: bash
         run: |
           export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/backup-work.sh" --once \
             2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/work-backup.log"
 
       - name: Snapshot audit/code on exit
         if: always()
         shell: bash
         run: |
           export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_ALL_CHATS=1 \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/snapshot-audit-code.sh" --once hub "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" \
             2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot-hub.log"
 
       - name: Clear the published session
         if: always()
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
           bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" 'slot=hub-windows' 'state=ended'
 
       - name: Save the models snapshot
         if: always()
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           try {
             $d = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/models/full' -TimeoutSec 20 -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'}
             $ms = @($d.models)
             $free = @($ms | Where-Object { $_.free })
             $obj = [ordered]@{
               kind = 'NPM-Hub'
               hubCount = $ms.Count
               hubFree = $free.Count
               hubTop = @($free | Select-Object -First 8 | ForEach-Object { $_.fullId })
               hubSelected = $d.selected
             }
             ($obj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4) | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\hub-models.json" -Encoding utf8
           } catch { }
           $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
           bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
             'slot=hub-windows' 'file=models-hub-windows.json' `
             'kind=NPM-Hub' 'os=windows' `
             "json=$env:TEMP\hub-models.json"
 
       - name: Export OpenCode chats for all repositories
         # Runs even on a cancelled/expired job so the NEXT windows run can
         # restore every repo's sessions (chats/<name>.json -> session-state).
         if: always()
         shell: bash
         run: |
           export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CHAT_ALL_ROOT="$HOME" PUBLISH=1 \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/export-chats.sh" --all \
             2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/export-chats.log"
 
       - name: Record the run in the history
         if: always()
         shell: pwsh
         run: |
           # history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/run-<runNumber>.json - see the Linux step.
           $env:GH_TOKEN = "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
           bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" journal=1 `
             "slot=hub-windows" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=windows" `
             "conclusion=${{ job.status }}" "endedAt=$([DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ'))" `
             "handoff=${{ inputs.handoff }}" `
             "runUrl=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
 
   # ── Linux Desktop VNC (parallel runner) ────────────────────────────────
   # A second, independent job next to `hub`. It stands up a headless Linux
   # desktop (openbox + xterm, Mesa software rendering) and exposes it through
   # x11vnc + noVNC + a cloudflared tunnel from the very start of the run, so
   # the hub gets a working graphical shell (an "Open the Linux screen" button)
   # without ever pressing Start. Kept alive by the same watchdog pattern as
   # the hub: dead desktop/tunnel gets restarted in-place.
   vnc:
     if: inputs.os == 'linux'
     runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_linux }}
     timeout-minutes: 360
 
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           path: fork
 
       - name: Install the desktop + VNC stack
         run: |
           sudo apt-get update -qq
           sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq \
             xvfb openbox xterm tint2 idesk x11vnc websockify novnc dbus-x11 \
             mesa-utils libgl1-mesa-dri libgl1 libegl1 libgles2 \
             libglu1-mesa libgbm1 x11-utils x11-xserver-utils \
             pcmanfm pulseaudio pavucontrol
 
       - name: Start the Linux desktop and open the tunnel
         run: |
           export VNC_PORT=5901 NOVNC_PORT=6081
           bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/start_desktop.sh" || {
             echo "::error::the Linux desktop VNC did not start."
             tail -30 $HUB_LOGS/xvfb.log $HUB_LOGS/openbox.log $HUB_LOGS/x11vnc.log 2>/dev/null
             exit 1
           }
 
           URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 6081 $HUB_LOGS/vnc-tunnel.log)
           if [ -z "$URL" ]; then
             echo "::error::no tunnel for the VNC desktop."
             tail -25 $HUB_LOGS/vnc-tunnel.log
             exit 1
           fi
           echo "$URL" > $HUB_LOGS/vnc-url
 
           # Pre-warm: the noVNC page must answer over the tunnel edge before
           # we hand the address to the panel.
           for i in $(seq 1 20); do
             code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -m 10 "$URL/vnc.html" || true)
             case "$code" in 2*|3*|4*) break ;; esac
             sleep 3
           done
 
           {
             echo "## Linux Desktop (VNC)"
             echo ""
             echo "**[Open the Linux screen]($URL/vnc.html)** - openbox + xterm + Mesa."
             echo ""
             echo "| | |"
             echo "|---|---|"
             echo "| noVNC | \`$URL/vnc.html\` |"
             echo "| VNC | \`127.0.0.1:5901\` (on the runner) |"
           } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
 
           echo "=================================================="
           echo " Linux Desktop VNC: $URL/vnc.html"
           echo "=================================================="
 
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
               "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
               "url=$URL/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$URL/vnc.html" \
               $([ -s "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" ] && echo "url2=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2")") \
               "label=${{ inputs.label }}"
 
           # Z11 dual tunnel on the desktop VM as well.
           nohup env GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/tunnel_keeper.sh" vnc >> "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.log" 2>&1 &
           echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.pid"
           echo "tunnel keeper: vnc endpoint now carries main + reserve addresses"
 
           # Same lifelines as the hub job (Z10): this VM holds the desktop the
           # user actually watches - when the hub VM wedges, the queue + tmate
           # here stay reachable. Beacons land in control/rescue-vnc.json and
           # control/heartbeat-vnc.json, commands pick target=vnc.
           if [ "${{ inputs.rescue_ssh }}" = "true" ]; then
             GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CONTROL_TARGET=vnc \
               nohup bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/rescue_ssh.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/rescue-ssh.log" 2>&1 &
             echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/rescue-ssh.pid"
             echo "rescue ssh daemon (vnc vm): -> control/rescue-vnc.json"
           fi
           if [ "${{ inputs.command_queue }}" = "true" ]; then
             GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CONTROL_TARGET=vnc \
               HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' \
               nohup bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/hub_control.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control.log" 2>&1 &
             echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control.pid"
             echo "control daemon (vnc vm): queue + heartbeat; reopen-tunnel reopens the VNC tunnel"
           fi
 
       - name: Keep the VNC session alive
         run: |
           PIDFILE="$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-6081.pid"
           cleanup_vnc() {
             local code="${1:-143}"
             trap - TERM INT
             if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
               local pid; pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
               [ -z "$pid" ] || kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
             fi
             pkill -f "websockify.*6081" 2>/dev/null || true
             pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:6081" 2>/dev/null || true
             # Background lifelines started above: same "Complete job" hang rule.
             pkill -f "[h]ub_control.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
             pkill -f "[r]escue_ssh.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
             pkill -f "[t]unnel_keeper.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
             rm -f "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-6081-reserve.pid" 2>/dev/null || true
             tmate -S "$HUB_LOGS/tmate.sock" kill-session >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
             # The X stack is started detached by start_desktop.sh and the
             # runner waits for it too - leaving Xvfb/openbox/x11vnc running
             # hangs "Complete job" exactly like the hub's daemons did.
             pkill -f "Xvfb ${VNC_DISPLAY:-:99}" 2>/dev/null || true
             pkill -f "[o]penbox" 2>/dev/null || true
             pkill -f "x11vnc.*${VNC_DISPLAY:-:99}" 2>/dev/null || true
             # Same as the hub job: `if: always()` does not survive a cancel.
             GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
               bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=vnc" "state=ended" \
               >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
             exit "$code"
           }
           trap 'cleanup_vnc 143' TERM INT
           VFAILS=0
           VRESTARTING=0
           for i in $(seq 1 1400); do
             sleep 15
             # Same rule as the hub watchdog: a busy CPU (a game or a build in
             # the desktop) can make one probe bleed over its timeout. Restart
             # the desktop only after several consecutive misses, and only if a
             # restart is not already in progress.
             if curl -sf -o /dev/null -m 20 "http://127.0.0.1:6081/vnc.html"; then
               VFAILS=0
             else
               VFAILS=$((VFAILS + 1))
               echo "::warning::VNC probe missed ($VFAILS consecutive)."
             fi
             if [ "$VFAILS" -ge 3 ] && [ "$VRESTARTING" = "0" ]; then
               echo "::warning::desktop VNC stopped answering; restarting it."
               VRESTARTING=1
               pkill -f "websockify.*6081" 2>/dev/null || true
               export VNC_PORT=5901 NOVNC_PORT=6081
               bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/start_desktop.sh" || true
               for boot in $(seq 1 12); do
                 if curl -sf -o /dev/null -m 20 "http://127.0.0.1:6081/vnc.html"; then
                   VFAILS=0; VRESTARTING=0
                   echo "::warning::VNC is back."
                   break
                 fi
                 sleep 5
               done
               if [ "$VRESTARTING" = "1" ]; then
                 echo "::warning::VNC did not come back; a later restart will retry."
                 VRESTARTING=0; VFAILS=0
               fi
             fi
             CUR=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url" 2>/dev/null || echo)
             PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || echo)
             if [ -n "$PID" ] && kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$CUR" ] \
               && bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/tunnel_health.sh" "$CUR" "/vnc.html"; then
               continue
             fi
             # Same stale-cloudflared cleanup as the hub job above; bracket
             # pattern so pkill never matches this shell's own command line.
             if [ -n "$PID" ] && kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
             pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:6081" 2>/dev/null || true
             sleep 1
             echo "::warning::VNC tunnel dead; reopening."
             URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 6081 $HUB_LOGS/vnc-tunnel2.log) || continue
             [ -n "$URL" ] || continue
             echo "$URL" > $HUB_LOGS/vnc-url
             echo "VNC back up on $URL/vnc.html"
             GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
               bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
                 "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
                 "url=$URL/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$URL/vnc.html" \
                 $([ -s "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" ] && echo "url2=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2")") \
                 "label=${{ inputs.label }}"
           done
           cleanup_vnc 0
 
       - name: Clear the published VNC session
         if: always()
         run: |
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=vnc" "state=ended"
 
       - name: Record the run in the history
         if: always()
         run: |
           # One small file per run, filed under the day and the weekday it
           # belongs to: history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/run-<runNumber>.json - the
           # diary the panel groups by day, and unlike the Actions UI it does not
           # disappear when GitHub prunes old runs.
           STARTED=""
           if [ -f "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" ]; then
             STARTED="$(date -u -d "@$(( $(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) / 1000 ))" '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || true)"
           fi
           GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
             bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" journal=1 \
               "slot=vnc" "kind=VNC" "os=linux" \
               "conclusion=${{ job.status }}" "endedAt=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" \
               ${STARTED:+journal_date="$STARTED"} \
               "handoff=${{ inputs.handoff }}" \
               "runUrl=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}" \
               2>&1 | tail -5 || echo "::warning::run history record failed"

 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 # tools/auto-ship.sh against a local bare repo standing in for GitHub.
 # No network. What is verified here is the behaviour that matters: it merges,
 # it does not merge red, and it refuses to report green for a suite that never
 # ran.
 set -uo pipefail
 HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
 TOOLS="$HERE/../tools"
 TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
 trap 'cd /; rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
 pass=0; fail=0
 check() { if [ "$2" = 1 ]; then pass=$((pass+1)); echo "PASS $1"; else fail=$((fail+1)); echo "FAIL $1"; fi; }
 
 # ── a bare "origin" and a working clone ──────────────────────────────────────
 git init -q --bare "$TMP/origin.git"
 mkdir -p "$TMP/w"
 git clone -q "$TMP/origin.git" "$TMP/w"
 ( cd "$TMP/w"
   git config user.email t@t; git config user.name t
   git checkout -q -b main 2>/dev/null || git checkout -q main
   echo base > base.txt; printf 'build/\nnode_modules/\n' > .gitignore
   git add -A; git commit -qm base; git push -q -u origin main )
 
 export HUB_LOGS="$TMP/logs"
 export AUTOSHIP_REPO="$TMP/w"

 # gh is absent in this sandbox too - it must degrade to commit+push and say so,
 # rather than silently claiming a PR exists.
 unset AUTOSHIP_BRANCH
 
 # gh is pretended away with AUTOSHIP_GH=0. Rewriting PATH would have been the
 # obvious way and it breaks the test itself: the script needs sh, grep, git and
 # the rest, and a PATH with only those in it breaks this harness too.
 export AUTOSHIP_GH=0
 
 # ── 1. red suite: the change is still pushed and committed, nothing claims green
 ( cd "$TMP/w" && echo change >> base.txt && mkdir -p build node_modules && echo built > build/out.o && echo big > node_modules/pkg.js )
 AUTOSHIP_TEST_CMD='sh -c "echo 3 passed, 1 failed; exit 1"' \
   bash "$TOOLS/auto-ship.sh" --once >/dev/null 2>&1
 check "red tests still commit" "$([ "$(git -C "$TMP/w" rev-list --count HEAD)" -gt 1 ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
 check "the work is pushed to its branch, not to main" "$(git -C "$TMP/origin.git" rev-parse --verify -q autoship >/dev/null && echo 1 || echo 0)"
 check "main was never pushed to directly" "$([ "$(git -C "$TMP/origin.git" rev-list --count main)" = 1 ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
 check "red run does not claim green" "$(grep -q 'tests RED' "$HUB_LOGS/auto-ship.log" && echo 1 || echo 0)"
 check "build output is not committed" "$(git -C "$TMP/w" ls-files | grep -qv 'build/out.o' && echo 1 || echo 0)"
 check "node_modules is not committed" "$(git -C "$TMP/w" ls-files | grep -qv 'node_modules' && echo 1 || echo 0)"

 # AUTOSHIP_TEST_CMD pointing at a missing binary: exit code is 127, which is
 # neither the green nor the red path, and must not be read as green.

   bash "$TOOLS/auto-ship.sh" --once >/dev/null 2>&1
 check "missing test binary is not reported green" "$(grep -q 'tests RED' "$HUB_LOGS/auto-ship.log" && echo 1 || echo 0)"
 check "missing test binary does not print tests green" "$(grep -q 'tests green' "$HUB_LOGS/auto-ship.log" && echo 0 || echo 1)"

   bash "$TOOLS/auto-ship.sh" --once >/dev/null 2>&1

 check "without gh it says so instead of faking a PR" "$(grep -q 'no gh: cannot open a PR' "$HUB_LOGS/auto-ship.log" && echo 1 || echo 0)"

 # and it returns non-zero when it cannot read a green CI state. So no merge.

+    # it main never moves, the work branch keeps diverging from it, and the
+    # fixture starts failing for reasons that have nothing to do with the script.

+    br_sha=$(git -C "$GH_STUB_W" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)

   bash "$TOOLS/auto-ship.sh" --once >/dev/null 2>&1

 check "the no-gh cases really ran without gh" "$(grep -qc 'no gh: cannot open a PR' "$HUB_LOGS/auto-ship.log" >/dev/null && echo 0 || echo 1)"

+GH_STUB_W="$TMP/w" GH_STUB_BARE="$TMP/origin.git" \

   bash "$TOOLS/auto-ship.sh" --once >/dev/null 2>&1

+GH_STUB_W="$TMP/w" GH_STUB_BARE="$TMP/origin.git" \

   bash "$TOOLS/auto-ship.sh" --once >/dev/null 2>&1
